neighbours.label: The English verb 'break' in any form and sense (break, breaks, broke, broken; break the glass, break the news, break a record, break up, break into, break free), firing on 'break' and the word right after it. Quiet for the noun 'break' (lunch break, spring break, coffee break) and for non-destructive verbs in the same frame (beat, open, block, fix). Other smashing verbs (smash, shatter) fire only weakly and are not part of the label.
fire: The toddler managed to break the glass vase before anyone could stop him.
She decided to break the news to her parents over dinner.
The sprinter hopes to break the world record at next month's championship.
After three years together, they decided to break up last spring.
Thieves tried to break into the warehouse around midnight.
The horse finally broke free of its rope and galloped across the field.
My laptop screen is broken, so I'm using my phone for now.
If you keep bending that ruler, it breaks in half.
quiet: The toddler managed to open the glass cabinet before anyone could stop him.
She decided to share the news with her parents over dinner.
The sprinter hopes to beat the world record at next month's championship.
After three years together, they planned a long trip last spring.
We took a coffee break around midnight before finishing the warehouse inventory.
The horse finally rested in the shade after galloping across the field.
My laptop screen is cracked, so I'm using my phone for now.
Students are heading to the beach for spring break this year.
